threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say you're headed to the 'city' like it's just a hop away, instead of bracing for a 45-minute Tube ride. Classic newbie move.
Caught a glimpse of a couple arguing over where to get off. He swore they’d just passed Brixton. She rolled her eyes and said, 'We just left it, you muppet.'

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy DJing from his balcony, while people in the street danced to his set. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you get a kebab at 3 AM and have it served by someone who breaks into a rap while preparing it.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot the fakes by their panic when BART's delayed—real ones just pull out headphones and settle in for the wait like it’s a normal Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 Balboa at 5:15, and the driver stopped to let a group of kids dance it out near the corner. Brief chaos, but that's SF for ya.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we all sip vermut at the same hour; locals know the best time is an hour before the bars close, for a true taste of Gràcia.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their insistence on asking locals where to find the 'best paella'—it’s the first sign they haven’t learned the tapas way yet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'—locals know there’s only one proper way to travel after dark.
Last week on the 36, someone brought a full chess set. Took up two seats but at least it sparked a game between two strangers. Only in Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a chef's apron juggling bratwursts outside the Kiezkneipe while the tram rumbled past—now that’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can catch a bus that’s just as likely to be delayed by a spontaneous street party as it is by a strike. Classic Berlin!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're local when you can name the coffee shop by the smell wafting from its door, not just the logo on the cup.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing an accordion on the 47 bus, but the real show was a cat in a carrier meowing along. No one batted an eye.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume we all sip on vermut by the hour, but locals really prefer a café con leche and a quick patat de Gràcia on a busy morning.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the 'l' and 'r' in 'Gràcia' – they still say it like it’s a tongue twister.
